subject: Dedicated commit — throughput validation matrix, measurement plan, and pricing path
messages:
From: Samira Khan <samira@cobaltapps.com>

Cc: sre@cobaltapps.com
Date: 2026-08-02T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated commit — capacity sizing and throughput guarantees

Hi Rafael,

Thanks for the earlier demo. We're finalizing procurement and need a clear acceptance path for Dedicated: specifically how you define and measure tokens/sec and request/sec guarantees, what latency targets apply, and how the measurement window maps to discounts/credits.

A few specifics from our SRE team:
- We expect to validate against a production-like mix (short chat messages ~32–128 tokens and long generation spikes up to 2k tokens).
- We need both a sustained tokens/sec guarantee (for steady throughput) and a request/sec/latency SLO for p95 and p99.
- Curious about how burst capacity is handled and whether cached prefixes or KV cache use is included in measurements.

Can you share a sample test plan and a pricing impact matrix (e.g., discount bands tied to measured throughput & latency)? We're trying to avoid blanket credits and want deterministic billing.

Thanks,
Samira
Director of Product, Cobalt Apps

Attachment: cobalt-throughput-profiles.xlsx (spreadsheet of request shapes)

From: rafael_mendes@redwood.ai
To: Samira Khan <samira@cobaltapps.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-08-03T10:08:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated commit — capacity sizing and throughput guarantees

Samira — really helpful asks, appreciate the clarity. High level reply, then I attached a concise acceptance & measurement playbook for your review.

Summary of Redwood proposal (short):
- Two-axis SLA: sustained tokens/sec (T/s) guarantee for reserved GPU pool and latency SLO (p95 response time) for a representative request mix.
- Measurement windows: 1-hour sustained sample for T/s (median of five 1-hour samples during a 7-day ramp window) and rolling 24-hour window for latency SLOs.
- Burst handling: customers get a configurable 1-hour burst bucket (extra T/s) per day; bursts measured separately and not counted toward sustained guarantee.
- Caching: prefix/KV cache counts toward observed throughput but we provide a second "cold-run" sample to normalize cache effects if the customer requests it.

Pricing/discount path (proposal):
- Baseline commit: reserved GPU pool for benchmarked T/s => standard list price.
- Band A (>=95% of guaranteed T/s and p95 <= target): 10% committed discount.
- Band B (>=90% and p95 within target + 30%): 5% discount.
- If observed <90% and remediation fails within 30 days, customer may receive 7 days pro-rated credits.

I attached: redwood-pricing-path-commit-v2.pdf (pricing matrix) and throughput-test-plan.csv (sample harness).

Next steps: if that looks reasonable, let's schedule a 60-min runbook walk-through with your SREs and our Solution Engineering team.

— Rafael
Rafael Mendes
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood-pricing-path-commit-v2.pdf, throughput-test-plan.csv

Rafael — thanks, the two-axis approach makes sense. A couple of clarifying Qs before the run-through:
1) For the 1-hour sustained sample median-of-five rule, can you share the exact traffic generator and seed inputs so our SREs can reproduce?
2) On cold-run normalization: if we opt for a cold-run, will we run it on identical hardware with a fresh model cache? If so, is that treated as the authoritative measurement or only an appendix?
3) Can you clarify the p95 target definition — is this end-to-end response time from HTTP request to final token emitted (streaming endpoints counted by final token)?

Also — would need a legal redline of contract language mapping the discount bands to measurement outcomes. Can you loop in Legal for the draft?

Samira

Rafael / team — draft runbook and agenda below (copying Samira for visibility). I kept it practical so we can run validation next week:

1) Objectives (10 mins) — confirm success criteria with SREs (sustained T/s target, p95 target, and sample conditioning).
2) Harness & seeds (10 mins) — I will share the exact k6 scripts, request mixes, and random seeds; harness will support short, medium, long shapes and a 10% cold-run mode.
3) Measurement method (15 mins) — we propose:
   - Sustained throughput: run three 1-hour contiguous trials during an 8-hour window; take the median T/s across trials as the measured sustained T/s.
   - Latency SLO: collect p95 & p99 across the same runs; streaming endpoints will be measured by time-to-final-token (TFT).
   - Cache normalization: run a single cold-run (cache cleared) for 30 minutes; if cold-run T/s differs >12% from warm-run, we present both numbers and default to warm-run for billing unless customer elects cold-run as authoritative.
4) Burst & bucket test (10 mins) — simulate a 1-hour burst at 150% of baseline to validate burst handling; bursts are not included in sustained calculation but must succeed without >5% error rate.
5) Acceptance & billing mapping (10 mins) — present discount band math and escalation steps.
6) Open Qs & next steps (5 mins).

Deliverables after run: raw logs, aggregated metrics (tokens/sec, req/sec, p95/p99), and a signed measurement report. We'll provide a DocuSign-ready quote with deal_id COB-2026-1141 once SREs sign off.

Samira — does that agenda work for you? If yes, we'll book a joint session and I'll attach the harness scripts (k6 + seed CSV).

— Marissa
Solutions Engineering, Redwood Inference

Attachments to come: throughput-test-harness-k6.tar.gz (scripts), measurement-report-template.xlsx
